stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes sterilization from disinfection of reusable healthcare items?

options.A: Sterilization and disinfection have the same microbial endpoint
options.B: Sterilization is limited to environmental surfaces and is not used for instruments
options.C: Sterilization destroys fewer microorganisms than high-level disinfection
options.D: Sterilization is intended to eliminate all forms of microbial life, whereas disinfection does not reliably eliminate all bacterial spores

rationale: CDC defines sterilization as a process that destroys or eliminates all forms of microbial life. Disinfection eliminates many or all pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate objects but, unlike sterilization, does not reliably eliminate bacterial spores. D is correct.
educational_objective: Differentiate the microbial endpoints of sterilization and disinfection.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization in Healthcare Facilities — Introduction, Methods, Definition of Terms
source_locator: Definition of Terms — Sterilization and Disinfection
source_claim_supported: Sterilization destroys/eliminates all forms of microbial life; disinfection eliminates many or all pathogenic microorganisms but not bacterial spores reliably.

source_original.stem: A nurse educator explains the difference between disinfection and sterilization to new staff, one of whom assumes the two terms are basically interchangeable ways of saying "very clean." The key distinction is instead that sterilization:

options.A: Sterilization and disinfection are interchangeable processes with the same microbial endpoint
options.B: Sterilization applies only to environmental surfaces and is not used for reusable instruments
options.C: Sterilization removes fewer microorganisms than high-level disinfection used on medical devices
options.D: Sterilization destroys all microbial life, including bacterial spores, unlike disinfection

source_original.rationale: Sterilization destroys all forms of microbial life, including highly resistant bacterial spores, representing the highest level of microbial elimination — used for items requiring the highest level of safety (such as surgical instruments). Disinfection eliminates most pathogenic microorganisms but does not reliably destroy all bacterial spores, making it appropriate for a different category of items/surfaces based on their intended use and infection risk (per the Spaulding classification).
source_original.source_detail: CDC disinfection/sterilization guideline: sterilization destroys all microbial life including bacterial spores; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Moved to CDC's exact definitions page, removed unnecessary Spaulding/application claims from the rationale, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy because this is a direct terminology distinction.

audit_findings.claim_audit: The definitions directly support the distinction in D.

distractor_audit.B: Sterilization is used for healthcare items/instruments, not only surfaces.

audit_findings.cueing: Shortened stem and kept alternatives parallel.
